documents.t: Excavate – Mine Smarter, Not Harder. Excavate introduces a smarter way to dig, mine, and chop in Minecraft Bedrock without breaking the vanilla balance or disabling achievements.  This add-on lets you break entire ore veins, tree clusters, or tunnels in one go, maintaining a stable tick performance by processing blocks progressively.  Players can fully customize which blocks are affected, define the maximum excavation range, and select from multiple mining shapes like Line, Tunnel, or Vein modes.  Excavate is designed to feel like an official vanilla feature — lightweight, configurable, and multiplayer-safe — making it the perfect quality-of-life addition for both survival and technical players.

UtilityCraft reshapes survival from the first day onward: start with simple tools and renewable resources, then grow into powered machines, storage, transport, and full automation.
Tiers decide which results are eligible, while multipliers increase output or the chance of successful rolls.

documents.t: Increase throughput before automation by expanding the Sieve setup and choosing the right efficiency tradeoff.

documents.s: Tools, pebbles, and your first Sieve.

After a pause, he returned in 2022 alongside WeatherVictor, officially founding Dorios Studios on September 9, 2022. During that period, the team worked on several addons inconsistently, taking extended breaks between projects. After a year-long hiatus, the team came back at the beginning of 2024, welcoming JRice as lead designer and texture artist. Together, they launched UtilityCraft 3.0, a milestone that gave the studio recognition within the Minecraft Bedrock community. Since then, more creators have joined the team, shaping Dorios Studios into the growing and passionate group it is today. Release Date: October 7, 2025 Developed by: Dorios Studios Download: UtilityCraft v3.2.0 on GitHub

UtilityCraft 3.2 delivers one of the most extensive updates to date, focusing on deeper automation, improved stability, and technical reworks for long-term addon compatibility. This release rebuilds core systems for machines, energy transfer, and fluid management, while introducing a new generator, refined UIs, and developer integration through ScriptEvents. Players can now enjoy more control, faster performance, and flexible automation that scales with their world.

Reworked sieving system with tiered meshes and balanced drop progression. Added Copper Cobblestone Generator as the first tier in a six-level structure. Rebalanced energy and speed across multiple machines including Crusher, Infuser, Digitizer, and Induction Anvil. New unified machine interface with progress display, upgrade slots, and information area.

Added the Wind Turbine, a passive generator whose efficiency varies with height. Generators now show detailed information such as time of day, remaining fuel, and efficiency. Introduced transfer modes for energy, items, and fluids: Nearest, Farthest, and Round.
Added Steel and Copper AiOTs, Hammers, and Paxels. Added Copper Mesh and new compressed item families. Updated textures for tools, machines, and Mob Grinder.
Mob Grinders are now upgradeable with Damage and Range modules. Can be toggled on or off for improved control. Enhanced entity detection and performance.

Full rewrite of machine, generator, and fluid systems for efficiency and modular design. Introduced ScriptEvent integration to allow external addons to register, replace, or modify recipes dynamically: utilitycraft:register_crusher_recipe utilitycraft:register_infuser_recipe utilitycraft:register_melter_recipe utilitycraft:register_crafter_recipe utilitycraft:register_fuel utilitycraft:register_sieve_drop Added utilitycraft:mesh component for defining custom sieve meshes. Updated rate speed settings: Super Fast → 2 ticks Fast → 4 ticks Normal → 10 ticks Slow (Default) → 20 ticks Super Slow → 40 ticks Reduced maximum stack size of upgrades to 8.

UtilityCraft 3.2 maintains full compatibility with other Dorios Studios projects and popular technical addons such as Integrated Storage and Drawers, ensuring a seamless automation network between systems.
For a detailed list of every addition, fix, and rework, visit the full changelog: UtilityCraft 3.2.0 | Full Changelog on GitHub

For documentation, setup guides, and detailed explanations, visit the official Dorios Studios Wiki: doriosstudios.com/docs/utilitycraft For updates, announcements, betas, and community discussions, join the Dorios Studios Discord: discord.gg/YvzPqJZTNd

This addon reimagines how players mine and gather resources. Instead of breaking blocks one by one, Excavate lets you instantly mine entire veins, trees, or tunnels — all while keeping lag to a minimum. Each block is processed with a short delay to maintain smooth performance even during large excavations, making it ideal for both survival and multiplayer servers.

Every player can fully customize their excavation experience: Add or remove blocks from your whitelist Toggle the excavate ability on or off Change your Shape Mode (Line, Tunnel, Vein, etc.) Adjust your Block Limit for performance and balance

One of Dorios Excavate’s strongest features is its compatibility with achievements. That means you can use it in your survival worlds without disabling Xbox Live achievements — making it perfect for both casual and competitive players.

Unlike traditional vein miners, Dorios Excavate was designed to be lag-friendly. By spreading block-breaking operations over short intervals, it ensures stable tick performance even when excavating massive areas.

Bountiful Trees introduces a new way to gather resources in Minecraft Bedrock — by growing them. This addon lets you cultivate trees made of ores, minerals, and gems, turning your farms into renewable sources of valuable materials while keeping a natural and immersive look. It blends farming and mining into a single, balanced progression system.
documents.s: Bountiful Trees – Grow Ores, Not Just Wood

documents.t: Each ore tree begins from a special sapling crafted with the mineral it represents. Once planted, it grows into a tree with a mineral-infused trunk and custom ore leaves. When fully grown, breaking the trunk yields both logs and ores, offering a decorative and practical alternative to mining. Ore trees grow just like vanilla saplings: They can grow naturally over time Or be instantly grown using Bone Meal No special tools or machines are required — simply plant, wait, and harvest.

Each ore sapling is crafted using: 1x Oak Sapling 8x of the corresponding mineral For example: Sapling Recipe Output Iron Sapling 1 Oak Sapling + 8 Iron Ingots Iron Ore Tree Diamond Sapling 1 Oak Sapling + 8 Diamonds Diamond Ore Tree Gold Sapling 1 Oak Sapling + 8 Gold Ingots Gold Ore Tree These recipes make ore trees a mid-to-late game feature, rewarding exploration and offering renewable ore production later on.

Ore trees feature trunks made of ore logs and unique leaves matching their mineral type. These leaves behave like vanilla ones, meaning they drop ore saplings, allowing continuous replanting and expansion. Breaking an ore tree’s trunk provides: Regular oak logs (as from normal trees) Ores or minerals depending on the sapling type Any standard tool can be used — harvesting is simple, familiar, and rewarding.

Bountiful Trees will soon feature full integration with UtilityCraft, allowing: Compact ore farming through Bonsai Pots Automation of harvesting and processing with UtilityCraft Machines Full energy-based systems powered by Dorios Energy (DE) This compatibility will make the addon ideal for both survival and technical players, offering natural progression and automation opportunities.

Tired of chopping trees or mining ores one block at a time? Excavate lets you break multiple connected blocks instantly while keeping the experience completely vanilla-friendly and achievements-compatible. This addon introduces a smarter way to dig, mine, and chop, processing each block with a short delay to keep performance stable and prevent lag during large excavations. Whether you want to clear entire ore veins, build tunnels, or fell trees in one go, Excavate gives you full control.

excavateadd – Adds a block to your personal excavate whitelist. excavateblacklistadd – Adds a block to the global blacklist. (Admin only) excavateblacklistremove – Removes a block from the global blacklist. (Admin only) excavatedefaultadd – Adds a block to the global default list. (Admin only) excavatedefaultremove – Removes a block from the global default list. (Admin only) excavatelimit – Sets your personal block limit for excavate. excavateopenmenu – Opens your personal excavate configuration menu. excavateremove – Removes a block from your personal excavate whitelist. excavateshape – Changes your current excavate shape or pattern. excavatetoggle – Toggles your excavate ability on or off.

Every player can personalize their excavation behavior using the in-game menu or commands. You can choose what blocks are excavatable, how far the ability reaches, and which shape defines your digging pattern.

Line – Mines straight forward, ideal for quick tunnels. Small Tunnel – Perfect 1×2 tunnels for easy exploration. Large Tunnel – Instantly clears a 3×3 path. Vein – Classic ore or tree vein mining mode (shapeless).

The configuration menu allows you to: Add or remove blocks from your personal whitelist Change your current Shape Mode Adjust your Block Limit Enable or disable excavation on demand Everything is designed for simplicity — quick setup, no command knowledge required.
Works seamlessly with achievements enabled worlds. Optimized to minimize lag on large operations.

Welcome to Ascendant Technology, the official end-game expansion for UtilityCraft. If UtilityCraft is your journey from basic survival to full automation, Ascendant Technology is what comes next: smarter logistics, more deliberate automation, and complex machines that reward planning instead of giant, messy farms. Ascendant Technology blends industrial progression with advanced tech and a minimal touch of fantasy, while staying grounded in UtilityCraft’s existing balance philosophy: powerful, but earned. Compatibility: Ascendant Technology is a DLC-style expansion and requires UtilityCraft installed.

Ascendant Technology extends UtilityCraft with late-game systems that interlock with its existing energy and automation loops. You’ll find: Multi-factorial Machines – Machines that use multiple inputs, catalysts, and even fluids, often producing residues and byproducts. Cryogenic System (Cryofluid) – A new coolant fluid used for stabilizing and cooling items and enabling advanced processing. New Materials – Late-game resources such as Titanium and Aetherium-chain items used in recipes and progression. Automation & Diagnostics – Better visibility into your factory with tools like the Network Center. Quality-of-Life UI – Dark-themed, modular UI components and per-machine interface improvements. Planned: Gases – A fourth “element” alongside items, energy, and fluids (coming in future updates). The goal is simple: automate more, with less world clutter, and give players who mastered UtilityCraft a new layer of depth.

Ascendant Technology focuses on end-game gameplay loops and infrastructure: Same Energy Standard (DE) No new power system to learn. Ascendant Technology machines run on Dorios Energy (DE) from UtilityCraft. Complex Machines, Real Payoff Machines like the Catalyst Weaver and Cryo Chamber introduce high-tier processing with multiple “layers” (catalysts, fluids, residues, temperature states). Factory Without Mega-Farms Build automation chains that reduce the need for giant, laggy farms—especially for rarer or more annoying resources. End & Nether Motivation Progression aims to give you more reasons to interact with The End and the Nether as part of your late-game upgrade path. Late-Game Logistics Heavy-duty storage blocks and diagnostics help keep complex setups understandable and maintainable. Cryofluid & Cooling Tech Cooling isn’t just cosmetic: it unlocks advanced processing and item state control.

Ascendant Technology is designed for players already established in UtilityCraft. A typical progression looks like this: Entry Point – Arrive with an established DE setup and late-game UtilityCraft infrastructure. Catalyst Weaver Era – Build the Catalyst Weaver and start producing early Ascendant materials (the gateway into the DLC). Aetherium Access – Unlock Aetherium chain recipes (used to push into higher-tier infrastructure and upgrades). Titanium & Cryogenics – Secure Titanium and build the Cryo Chamber to create Cryofluid, stabilize volatile items, and unlock cooling-based recipes. Factory Visibility – Add tools like the Network Center (and other late-game logistics) to keep your systems readable and scalable. High-End Machines – Expand into machines like the Liquifier and Singularity Fabricator, where planning and resource flow matter as much as raw power. Future Updates – Gases and deeper multi-system automation loops. Each step is meant to feel like a real upgrade to your factory—without replacing the fun of survival.
GitHub Releases More download mirrors (MCPEDL / CurseForge) will be added after the public release.

The Better Smelters addon introduces a variety of improved furnaces crafted from ores and rare materials. Each tier smelts faster and consumes less fuel, allowing players to process resources more efficiently as they progress through the game. These upgraded smelters can be used manually or fully automated using hoppers, chests, and other item transport systems.

Furnace Tier Fuel Consumption Smelting Speed Oak Wood Furnace 1.0x Normal Copper Furnace 1.0x 1.5x Iron Furnace 1.0x 2x Netherrack Furnace 0x 2x Gold Furnace 0.8x 3x Emerald Furnace 0.6x 5x Diamond Furnace 0.4x 10x Amethyst Furnace 0.4x 15x Netherite Furnace 0.2x 20x Blazing Furnace 0.1x 25x Nether Star Furnace 0.01x 10x (1 Stack per Cycle) ⚠ Lower fuel consumption means fuel lasts longer. For example, a furnace with 0.1x fuel consumption gets 10x more smelts per fuel item than a regular furnace.

Smelters function exactly like vanilla furnaces but support full automation: Input items: Pulled automatically from the container on the left. Fuel: Pulled from the top container. Output: Sent to the container on the right, if there’s space. This system allows you to set up complete smelting lines that run on their own.
The Netherite Furnace can be crafted using either a Diamond Furnace or an Amethyst Furnace as part of the recipe.

The Netherrack Furnace does not consume fuel. The Wood Furnace disappears after a few minutes of use. Supports full automation with hoppers and containers. Perfect for large-scale smelting setups or late-game automation bases.

Bountiful Bonsais is a lightweight addon designed to make your life easier by automating the production of basic natural resources — such as wood, plants, and crops — without breaking survival balance. Instead of farming manually, you can grow small bonsai trees that passively generate drops over time. Each bonsai can be customized with different soils, trees, and crops, affecting both the growth speed and type of resources produced.

🌳 Grow trees and crops automatically 🪴 Use different soils to adjust growth time ⚙️ Integrate with UtilityCraft containers for full automation 💎 Discover 26 unique bonsai types covering every tree and crop from Minecraft Each bonsai grows over time and drops its resources directly into the container below (such as a chest or barrel). No hoppers are required — making early automation simple and efficient.

To start using bonsais, you’ll need to craft a Bonsai Pot, place it over a container, and plant a sapling or seed along with a compatible soil. Once placed, it will automatically begin producing items every growth cycle. Continue to Crafting and Setup →
Before your bonsai can start producing resources, you’ll first need to craft a Bonsai Pot and understand how it works.

The Bonsai Pot is the core block of the addon. It acts as the growing platform where all bonsais are planted. Recipe: 3 × Stone Slabs 1 × Hopper 2 × Planks Once crafted, it’s ready to be placed anywhere.

Place your bonsai on top of a container, such as a Chest or Barrel. This allows it to automatically store all generated items — no hopper is required. Each bonsai collects its drops directly in the block beneath it. You can use any container that supports item storage, including UtilityCraft blocks.
Every bonsai requires a soil to grow. Different soils affect growth speed and compatibility with plants.

Soil Type Effect Dirt / Grass Normal growth Red Sand / Sand 10s faster Hoed Soil Additional 10s faster Using a hoe on soil increases growth speed — except on special soils from UtilityCraft or Bountiful Crops, which already have unique properties.

Soil Type Compatible Plants Dirt / Grass Vanilla trees, crops, berries, mushrooms Sand / Red Sand Cactus, Sugar Cane, Kelp Crimson Nylium Crimson Tree Warped Nylium Warped Tree Endstone Chorus Fruit Soul Sand Nether Wart The base growth time for any bonsai is 60 seconds, reduced further by certain soils and upgrades.

Once you’ve added soil, take a sapling or seed and interact with the bonsai to plant it. If placed correctly, a miniature version of the plant will appear. Your bonsai will now begin to grow and automatically produce resources. 💡 Tip: You don’t need a hopper below the bonsai. It will automatically transfer items to the container beneath it.
You can remove: Only the bonsai using shears (keeps the soil) Both bonsai and soil by sneaking and breaking it with your hand

Now that your bonsai is producing items, it’s time to understand how growth mechanics and loot work — including drop rates, special soils, and how to fully automate your setup. Continue to Growth & Drops →
Every bonsai follows a simple cycle: grow → harvest → repeat. The type of soil, the plant, and certain modifiers directly affect the growth speed and loot outcome.

By default, each bonsai takes 60 seconds to complete a full growth cycle. However, this time can be reduced with better soils or certain actions. Modifier Effect on Growth Sand / Red Sand -10 seconds Hoed Soil -10 seconds Special Soils (UtilityCraft) Varies per type Some soils can multiply the output or cut the growth time in half, depending on their tier.

When combined with UtilityCraft or Bountiful Crops, you gain access to special soils that greatly boost bonsai performance. These soils cannot be hoed and each offers unique benefits. Soil Bonus Loot Multiplier 🟡 Yellow Soil Faster growth ×1.5 🔴 Red Soil Even faster growth ×2 🔵 Blue Soil Double output ×2 ⚫ Black Soil Maximum output ×4 💡 Tip: Higher-tier soils not only shorten growth time, but also multiply the amount of drops produced by your bonsais.

Each bonsai generates resources once its growth cycle completes. The type and amount of loot depend on the bonsai type, soil, and RNG. Bonsai Type Main Drop Side Drops Special Notes Trees Logs Leaves, Sticks, Saplings Most common bonsai type Crops Crops / Seeds — Simple and fast-growing Mushrooms Mushrooms — Grows faster in dark Bamboo / Cactus Plant Items — Best for bulk farming Chorus / Nether Plants Rare materials — Longer growth time All drops are automatically inserted into the container below the bonsai (Barrel, Chest, or compatible block). You can chain multiple containers or connect them with UtilityCraft hoppers or uppers for transport.

Every bonsai calculates its total output like this: Base Drops × Soil Multiplier For example: A Dirt Bonsai might yield 6–10 logs. The same bonsai on Blue Soil could yield up to 20. On Black Soil, it can reach 40 or more per cycle.

Bountiful Crops is part of the UtilityCraft collection and introduces a new way to obtain resources — through 31 different crops that grow materials like iron, gold, slime, diamond, and even Nether Stars. Each crop belongs to a specific tier and must be planted on its corresponding Soil block.
Crops behave similarly to vanilla ones but with tier-based mechanics. Higher-tier crops yield rarer materials and require upgraded soils to grow.

Tier Soil Color Description Tier 1 Yellow Soil Basic crops like coal, copper, and water. Tier 2 Red Soil Mid-tier crops like iron, lapis, and slime. Tier 3 Blue Soil Advanced crops like diamond, emerald, and quartz. Tier 4 Black Soil Endgame crops like Nether Star and Wither Skull. Crops require the correct soil tier to grow. Using a hoe reduces growth time by 10 seconds, except for special soils.
All crops start from a Base Seed, which can then be upgraded into specific crop seeds using their respective materials.

Each crop produces its respective resource and can benefit from Fortune enchantments. Fortune III significantly increases drop quantity. Crop Drop Fortune Affected Iron Crop Iron Ingot ✅ Diamond Crop Diamond ✅ Gold Crop Gold Ingot ✅ Redstone Crop Redstone Dust ✅ Lapis Crop Lapis Lazuli ✅ Nether Star Crop Nether Star ✅ Wither Skull Crop Wither Skeleton Skull ✅

Some unique crops provide special items instead of basic minerals: Crop Drop Use Water Crop Water Ball Places water and substitutes water buckets in recipes. Lava Crop Lava Ball Places lava and can substitute lava buckets. Obsidian Recipe 2 Lava Balls + 2 Water Balls Creates Obsidian.
Players receive a Guide Book upon entering a world with Bountiful Crops installed. It contains detailed information about all soils, seeds, and crafting recipes. If lost, you can craft a new one:

Bountiful Crops connects directly with other UtilityCraft systems: Crops can be harvested automatically using the Harvester. Soils are compatible with Bountiful Bonsais for passive crop farming. Items like Lava and Water Balls can fuel or interact with UtilityCraft machines. This addon extends the automation potential of UtilityCraft, turning farming into a renewable source of valuable materials.

Tired of mining for cobblestone? Now you can automate the process with Cobblestone Generators, a standalone add-on that also comes integrated within UtilityCraft. It provides a simple and efficient way to generate unlimited cobblestone automatically, perfect for early automation setups or standalone skyblock-style worlds.
There are 5 tiers of Cobblestone Generators: Iron, Gold, Emerald, Diamond, and Netherite. Each tier increases production speed, allowing faster and more efficient cobble generation.

To get started, craft the first-tier generator using the recipe below. You can later upgrade it all the way up to Netherite (requires Netherite Scrap). Each tier slightly increases the production speed of the generator allowing faster cobblestone output as you progress through the materials.

Each generator has a conduit port on one side — this indicates where items are output. Place a container (like a chest or barrel) in front of that side to collect the cobblestone. They can be placed facing any direction, giving flexibility for automation setups. If no container is connected, the generator can hold up to 64 cobblestones internally, and you can collect them by hand.

Tier Speed (Cobblestone per Second) Iron 0.5 Gold 1 Emerald 2 Diamond 4 Netherite 20 The higher the tier, the faster the generator. The last tier produces cobblestone so quickly that you’ll soon need better storage solutions.

When storage becomes a problem, you can use Compressed Cobblestone. It allows you to save space by combining 9 cobblestones into 1 compressed version and you can compress up to 9 times! Example Recipe Result Compressing 9 Cobblestone 1 Compressed Cobblestone Decompressing 1 Compressed Cobblestone 9 Cobblestone Compressing cobblestone helps reduce clutter and manage large-scale production efficiently. If you reach nonuple compressed cobblestone, you’ve processed over 43 million blocks — good luck getting there!

Dorios' Basics is part of the UtilityCraft addon pack and focuses on improving early-game survival and resource gathering. It introduces tools like Pebbles, Hammers, Sieves, Crucibles, and Sinks — essential mechanics for Skyblock-style starts or minimalist progression worlds. This module provides the foundation for UtilityCraft’s early progression loop. Players can generate resources from minimal materials and automate their basic survival setups.

Use a Wooden or Stone Hammer while sneaking and interacting with the ground to collect small fragments called Pebbles. These can be recombined into full blocks, making it possible to rebuild stone resources even in Skyblock-like environments. Source Block Pebble Type Grass / Dirt Dirt Pebble Stone Stone Pebble Gravel Gravel Pebble Granite Granite Pebble Diorite Diorite Pebble Andesite Andesite Pebble

Hammers are the cornerstone of resource progression. They allow players to break blocks down into smaller materials: Input Output Cobblestone Gravel Gravel Dirt Dirt Sand Netherrack Crushed Netherrack Cobbled Deepslate Crushed Deepslate End Stone Crushed End Stone Combine hammers with Sieves for optimal ore farming.

Craft Flint using 3 Gravel directly in your inventory, then make a Flint Knife. Use it to harvest Plant Fibers from leaves. Combine 3 Fiber → String Enables early crafting recipes before you can hunt spiders.

The Mortar extracts water from saplings and is essential for early hydration. Crafting Recipe: 3 Cobblestone 1 Stone Pebble Usage: Place 2 Saplings, 1 Glass Bottle, and 1 Mortar in your inventory crafting grid to create a Water Bottle. The mortar is not consumed.

The Sieve filters blocks such as gravel, dirt, or sand to extract valuable materials and seeds. Place a mesh inside, add a siftable block on top, and start filtering! Works in groups up to 5x5 (25 sieves total). Interacting with one activates all adjacent sieves at once.

Use the Crucible to convert cobblestone into Lava or Obsidian using different heat sources. Heat Source Strength Torch 1 Fire / Campfire / Magma 2 Soul Fire / Soul Torch 3 Lava 4 Place cobblestone in the crucible, wait for it to melt, then collect with a bucket.
Crafting a Sink gives you an infinite water source, perfect for automated crops and machine setups.
Dorios’ Basics is the first module in the UtilityCraft progression chain, providing the groundwork for later automation, energy systems, and advanced machinery.

The Dorios' Trinkets addon introduces a collection of over 80 unique trinkets — rings, amulets, charms, pendants, and more — each designed to grant special abilities and stat boosts that enhance your adventures across the world of Minecraft. With a dedicated trinket inventory system, players can equip and manage their accessories seamlessly. From extra health and speed to magic protection and life steal, every trinket brings new strategic depth to gameplay.
Trinkets can be equipped through a custom inventory menu or directly from your hand. To access the inventory, interact while holding the Trinket Scroll, craftable using paper.

The addon includes 13 unique slots for maximum customization: Slot Type Examples Head Helmets, Masks Necklace Pendants, Amulets Body Emblems, Quivers Feet Boots Rings Normal and Heavy Rings Charms Abyssal Orbs, Purity Blossoms Talismans Holy Cross, Bloodgem Gauntlets Fire, Ice, Venom variants Dolls Voodoo-type trinkets Amulets Bloodbound, Abyssal Sun, etc.

Tier Description Primitive Basic trinkets with simple effects, ideal for early-game. Apprentice Intermediate trinkets with stronger abilities. Mastercraft Advanced trinkets offering powerful effects. Ascendant Top-tier trinkets with game-changing bonuses. Ascendant+ Beyond Ascendant – the rarest and strongest trinkets. Responsive stat bonuses stack dynamically. Example: +10 health and -2 health trinkets result in a total of +8 health.

Trinkets provide a variety of benefits and powers, such as: Increased health, damage, and speed Enhanced water mobility and magic protection Life steal during combat Immunity to negative status effects Item repair and double jump abilities
Trinkets can be found, looted, or crafted throughout the world:
Dorios' Trinkets is fully compatible with: Archaism Talismans Archaism Trinkets Amulets Vanilla They share the same core system, allowing combined use without issues.
Works on Minecraft Bedrock 1.21.50+ Does not require experimental toggles Uses a player.json-based stat system for all bonuses 100% compatible with multiplayer and realms

Effect Pillars is a modular beacon-style system included in the UtilityCraft collection. It introduces customizable Pillars that grant unique effects — both supportive and offensive — far beyond what vanilla beacons can do. By combining Upgrades, Amplifiers, and Effect Beacons, players can build pillars with adjustable range and power levels. These structures can protect your base, enhance your abilities, or even repel hostile mobs automatically.

Effect Pillars are built using a simple vertical structure made of three parts: Upgrade Block – Defines the effect level. Amplifier Block – Determines the radius of the effect. Effect Beacon – Determines which effect the pillar will emit. All components must be placed in the correct order for the pillar to activate.

These determine how powerful the effect will be — similar to beacon levels. Upgrade Type Effect Level Example Redstone Upgrade Level 1 Basic strength or speed Glowstone Upgrade Level 2 Medium power boost Amethyst Upgrade Level 3 Maximum strength

The Amplifier determines how far the pillar’s effect reaches. Amplifier Type Range (Blocks) Iron Amplifier 25 Gold Amplifier 50 Diamond Amplifier 75 Netherite Amplifier 100 Nether Star Amplifier 250 Amplifiers must be placed on top of the Upgrade block.

Placed at the top of the pillar, these define which effect is granted or applied. There are two main categories: Supportive Effects (Blue Beacons): Affect players and allies. Offensive Effects (Red Beacons): Target only hostile mobs, ideal for base defense. Example Effect Type Description Speed Support Increases player movement speed. Strength Support Boosts attack power. Regeneration Support Gradually restores health. Poison Aura Offensive Damages nearby mobs. Weakness Field Offensive Reduces enemy attack damage.
All components are crafted using the Base Stone, a key ingredient used across recipes.
When entering a world for the first time, you’ll receive a Guide Book explaining all recipes and effects. If lost, it can be crafted again easily.

Redstone Lamps Plus is a Dorios Studios addon that ports the classic Java Edition Redstone Lamps to Minecraft Bedrock — enhanced with full RTX lighting and Vibrant Visuals shader support. It provides beautiful, responsive lighting for both technical and decorative builds across all devices.

This add-on faithfully reproduces the behavior of Redstone Lamps from Java Edition, while improving visuals and compatibility. The lamps can be powered by any redstone signal source and will turn off when power is removed.

Place a Redstone Lamp. Apply power (lever, button, torch, comparator, repeater, etc.). The lamp lights up when powered. Remove power to turn it off. Lighting dynamically adapts to RTX or Vibrant Visuals if enabled.
When RTX is enabled, Redstone Lamps emit realistic, physically-based lighting and reflections. They blend perfectly with metallic or glass-based builds.
If you play on mobile or non-RTX platforms, the lamps automatically use Vibrant Visuals, a new experimental shader option that provides high-quality illumination without ray tracing.
Game Version: Minecraft Bedrock 1.21.100+ RTX Ready: ✅ Vibrant Visuals: ✅ Experimental Toggles: ❌ Not required Platforms: Windows, Console, and Mobile
This is an unofficial Bedrock port of the original Java Edition Redstone Lamps Plus by LicitLettuce, adapted and optimized by Dorios Studios for cross-platform lighting.

The Training Dummy is part of the UtilityCraft collection and serves as a practical testing tool for players. It allows you to accurately measure your damage output (DMG) or damage per second (DPS) depending on the mode it’s set to. Ideal for addon developers, RPG systems, or players fine-tuning their builds — the dummy provides an exact numeric reading of your performance during combat, helping you optimize your damage and attack rhythm.

The dummy is a stationary target that detects hits from weapons, trinkets, or abilities. It calculates the amount of damage dealt and can switch between two modes: Mode Description DMG Mode Displays total damage per hit. DPS Mode Displays damage per second across multiple hits. You can toggle modes by interacting with the dummy (right-click / interact button).

Real-time damage tracking. Switchable modes (DMG / DPS). Works with melee, ranged, and custom scripted weapons. Compatible with Dorios' Trinkets and other UtilityCraft combat systems. Does not require experimental options — works on stable versions of Minecraft.

Welcome to UtilityCraft, an addon pack built to turn the grind of survival into something smarter, smoother, and a lot more fun. Here, effort transforms into efficiency: chop less, mine less, and let machines, generators, and bonsais do the heavy lifting while you focus on the adventure. UtilityCraft is designed with balance in mind. It won’t hand you overpowered shortcuts, but it will give you the tools to automate the boring parts, expand your resource options, and build real factory-style setups in Minecraft Bedrock. Think of it as your path from basic survival to full automation—without ever breaking the survival feel. This is the first step in the series: From Dirt to Steel, where you’ll move from pebbles and sieves to the foundations of your first machines.

UtilityCraft isn’t just one addon—it’s a bundle of systems that all connect together. You’ll find: Bountiful Bonsais – Passive farming for wood and crops. Bountiful Crops – Grow ores and rare resources in fields. Cobblestone Generators – Infinite cobble, from basic iron speed up to blazing netherite. Mechanical Spawners – Customizable mob farming. Dorios' Basics – Core blocks, recipes, and progression tools. Fluid Tanks – Store and move huge amounts of liquids. Paxels & AIOTs – Multi-tools to save space and time. Way Computer – A step into automation and digital systems. Each piece on its own is useful, but together they create a complete tech progression for survival.

UtilityCraft is built around a few core systems that tie everything together: Energy System Everything runs on Dorios Energy (DE). You’ll generate power with furnaces, lava, sunlight, and more, then store it in batteries and feed it into your machines. Machines Crushers, infusers, presses, furnaces, harvesters, and more. Each machine has upgrades to speed it up, make it more efficient, or expand its range. Item Transportation Move items with improved hoppers, uppers, and automation blocks, or go advanced with conduits and exporters. Blocks and Items From compressed cobblestone to special crafting components, UtilityCraft introduces new building blocks and crafting materials that push progression forward. Mechanics New farming systems, bonsai growth mechanics, mob spawning tweaks, liquid generation, and more—all designed to slot naturally into Minecraft’s survival loop. Useful Recipes Tons of new recipes and tweaks so that resources and progression always feel smooth.

UtilityCraft is all about gradual progression. You’ll start small and build up: Early Game – Pebbles, sieves, and flint tools. Resource Farming – Bonsais, cobblestone generators, and crops. First Steps to Steel – Craft steel with SmeltFlare and unlock the Workbench. The Machinery Era – Begin crafting machines, generators, and setting up energy systems. Automation – Link machines together, automate resource chains, and design your own survival factory. This way, every step feels earned and every upgrade unlocks something new.
MCPEDLCurseForge

After mastering your first Sieve and Hammer, it’s time to scale up and expand your resource generation. This section focuses on efficiency — faster sieving, better meshes, and preparing for the next stage of automation.

To gather more materials efficiently, you can place multiple Sieves next to each other in a 5x5 grid. Up to 25 Sieves can work simultaneously, allowing you to process entire stacks of Gravel or Dirt at once. Each Sieve works independently but can use different meshes, letting you mix drop types. The next tier of mesh is Flint, crafted using Gravel. Collect extra Gravel early — it will be essential for faster progression and better drop chances.

Wood is crucial for crafting and expanding your sieving stations. One of the best ways to get large amounts quickly is by sieving Dirt until you obtain Jungle Saplings. Jungle trees are tall and dense, giving you far more wood than normal ones. To make things even easier, you can craft an AIOT (All-In-One Tool). When sneaking, it activates Tree Capitation, letting you break entire trees instantly. Still, manual farming takes time… and that’s where Bonsais enter the stage — your first step toward automated tree farming.

Once you have a steady resource flow, it’s time to upgrade your meshes. Higher-tier meshes significantly increase your chances of getting rare ores and unique drops. Each tier refines the results, giving more efficient yields per block. Mesh progression goes as follows: String Mesh Flint Mesh Copper Mesh Iron Mesh Gold Mesh Emerald Mesh Diamond Mesh Netherite Mesh Each tier improves the range of resources obtainable from Gravel, Dirt, and Sand. Upgrade progressively as your world expands to ensure a continuous flow of valuable materials.

To speed up production, you can compress materials like Cobblestone and Gravel. Compressed blocks can then be hammered or sieved for faster bulk processing. The fastest method involves crafting Compressed Cobblestone, hammering it into Compressed Gravel, and continuing until you reach Compressed Sand. This process saves time and inventory space, helping you prepare for large-scale sieving and the upcoming use of machines and generators. With stronger meshes, efficient tree farming, and compressed materials, you now control the pace of your progression. At this stage, it’s recommended to explore Bountiful Bonsais — it introduces automated tree farming that pairs perfectly with your growing setup. From here, you’re ready to move beyond manual labor and into Water & Lava Production →, the next step toward full automation in UtilityCraft.

You’ve mastered resource gathering, water and lava production, and cobblestone generation. Now it’s time to take your first steps into metallurgy — creating Steel. This marks the beginning of your transition into the Machinery Era.

To start producing Steel, you’ll need Raw Iron, Coal, and a new item called the SmeltFlare. The SmeltFlare lets you combine raw materials directly in your inventory to craft metal alloys. But wait — Paper? To obtain it, sieve Dirt to get Sugar Cane, then craft it into Paper. You’ll need this to complete your SmeltFlare recipe.

Once you have a SmeltFlare, place it in your inventory along with Raw Iron and Coal. The SmeltFlare will merge them into Brute Steel, a raw alloy that can later be refined. Once you’ve made Brute Steel, smelt it in a Furnace or use another SmeltFlare to produce Steel Ingots. Tip: Combine 9 Brute Steel into a Brute Block to smelt 9 ores at once — this speeds up the process dramatically.

Before diving into advanced machinery, you’ll need to craft a Workbench. This specialized crafting table is used to create machines, generators, and upgrades. You’re officially entering the Machinery Era.

Before proceeding, make sure you’ve collected: Enough Steel and Iron for machine crafting Copper and Redstone (obtained by sieving Sand) Optional: Coal and Brute Blocks for efficient smelting You now have everything you need to begin crafting machines and stepping into UtilityCraft’s automation systems. Next: learn how to build your first powered machines in the next section — Machinery Basics.
UtilityCraft transforms early survival into a smoother, more rewarding experience. This guide walks you through the first steps — from collecting pebbles to setting up your first sieve.

Every journey in UtilityCraft begins with your first hammer, the tool that transforms the world around you. At the beginning, you won’t be able to mine stone directly. Instead, you’ll need to craft a Wooden Hammer (or a Stone one if you already advanced a bit) and use it in a clever way. To get your first resources, sneak and interact (right-click or long-press) on Dirt or Grass Blocks while holding your hammer. Each interaction will drop small fragments called Pebbles, which represent different kinds of base materials. These can include: Dirt Pebbles Gravel Pebbles Stone Pebbles Andesite, Granite, and Diorite Pebbles And occasionally Bone Meal, which helps accelerate your early growth Once you collect enough Pebbles, combine 4 of the same type in a crafting grid to make Cobblestone, your first renewable building block. Before you can start gathering Pebbles, you’ll first need to craft the Wooden Hammer. It’s made using simple materials from your first tree: planks, logs, and sticks. This hammer will be one of your most useful tools early on. Besides letting you collect Pebbles, it can also break blocks into smaller forms later in the game (Cobblestone → Gravel → Dirt → Sand), which will become essential for sieving. This is the recipe. Remember to save at least one log from your first tree, since you’ll need it to craft the hammer and begin your first steps in UtilityCraft.
With Cobblestone and Wood secured, it is time to craft your first important tools. These will let you gather string and begin filtering blocks for valuable resources.

The Flint Knife is one of the first special tools you will need. By using it on Leaves, you can collect Plant Fibers, which can then be crafted into String. String is essential for your first meshes and later for more advanced recipes. If you don’t have Flint, remember you can craft it by combining 3 Gravel. This makes the Flint Knife accessible very early, even before exploring caves. Once you start cutting leaves, you will gather Plant Fibers. These can be crafted directly into String, which is one of the most important ingredients in UtilityCraft. Without String you won’t be able to make your first Mesh, and therefore your Sieve will remain useless. Crafting Recipes​

Once you have String, the next step is to craft a Sieve. The Sieve will allow you to filter blocks like Gravel, Dirt, or Sand into useful resources, such as ores, seeds, and rare drops. At this stage, it becomes one of your most valuable tools for progression. To keep wood production steady, you can use Bone Meal on Saplings, helping you farm planks faster and maintain a supply for crafting. The Sieve requires a Mesh to work. Start with the String Mesh, then upgrade later into stronger meshes that improve drop chances.

Your Sieve will not work on its own — it needs a Mesh. The very first one you can make is the String Mesh, crafted with sticks and string. This will be the key to turning ordinary blocks into valuable early-game resources. Once crafted, simply place the mesh into the Sieve by interacting with it. From this point, you can start filtering blocks like Gravel, Dirt, and Sand to extract ores, seeds, and other drops that will fuel your progression.

The Hammer plays a crucial role in this stage. It allows you to reduce blocks step by step, each stage unlocking new possibilities for sieving: Cobblestone → Gravel Gravel → Dirt Dirt → Sand This chain means you can recycle almost anything back into useful resources. By combining Hammering with Sieving, even the most basic blocks become a renewable source of progression.

Now that your Sieve has a String Mesh, try placing Gravel inside. This will begin producing small amounts of Coal, Iron pieces, and other basic drops. As you advance, upgrading to stronger meshes will improve the drop chances and unlock rarer materials. At this point, you now have the basic loop of Hammer → Sieve → Resources. This is the foundation of UtilityCraft’s progression: turning simple blocks into the materials that will eventually lead you to automation and machines. At this stage of your journey, you should already have the basics in place: A Wooden or Stone Hammer for breaking blocks down A Flint Knife to turn leaves into string A Sieve equipped with your first String Mesh With these tools, you now have steady access to String, Gravel, Dirt, and Sand, and you’ve learned how to sieve them for your very first ores, seeds, and useful drops. This marks the foundation of UtilityCraft’s progression: turning simple blocks into a growing supply of resources. From here, you’re ready to take the next step — expanding your production and unlocking new ways to automate survival. Continue to Expanding Resources →
In this chapter, you’ll learn how to produce Water and Lava, two essential resources for progressing in UtilityCraft. These materials unlock early automation, farming, and even Nether access.

Begin by crafting a Mortar using 3 Cobblestone and 1 Stone Pebble. Use the Mortar along with 1 Glass Bottle and 2 Saplings to create a Water Bottle. The Mortar won’t be consumed in the process. Once you have 3 Water Bottles, place a Cauldron and use the bottles to fill it. When it’s full, use a Bucket to collect your first Water Bucket.

To generate lava, you’ll need a Crucible. It converts Cobblestone into Lava over time. The Crucible must be placed above a heat source — such as a Torch, Campfire, Fire, or Lava. Heat Source Strength Lava / Flowing Lava 4 Soul Fire / Torch / Campfire 4 Fire 3 Campfire 3 Magma Block 3 Torch 1 Stronger heat sources speed up the conversion. Feeding 4 Cobblestone into the Crucible will slowly generate 1 bucket of Lava. You can also interact with the Crucible using a Water Bucket to instantly create Obsidian, useful for early Nether access.

To craft a Crucible, you’ll need 4 Bricks and 3 Mud Bricks. Bricks are made by smelting Clay, which you can obtain by sieving Sand. To make Mud Bricks, start by creating Mud: place Dirt and use a Water Bottle on it to convert it. Then combine the Mud with Wheat to make Packed Mud. Use 4 Packed Mud in a Crafting Table to create 1 Mud Brick. Wheat Seeds are obtained by sieving Dirt. Once you have both Bricks and Mud Bricks, craft your Crucible. With a stable source of Water and Lava, you’ve unlocked the foundation for energy generation and automation. Next, we’ll move toward creating Cobblestone Generators and understanding early power systems in UtilityCraft. Continue to Cobblestone Generation →

The wiki reuses small, original game sprites alongside visible labels. WikiIcon renders a decorative square image with nearest-neighbour display and an SVG fallback for unmapped concepts. It respects the Docusaurus base URL and never changes the block/item artwork.

Ascendant Technology: RP/textures/ui/at_icons/*.png, 16×16. The shared library now contains 47 sprites, including the 20 already used for machine resources. Existing URLs remain unchanged under /img/addons/ascendant/resources/glyphs/. Local vanilla resource pack: resource_pack/textures/ui/*_effect.png, 18×18. The 33 individual effects are stored under /img/wiki/ui/effects/. frozen_effect.png is an overlay and is deliberately excluded. Both sets are copied byte-for-byte. No resampling, format conversion or AI generation is involved. Do not use the small glyphs as large hero artwork. Run npm run generate:wiki-ui-icons from website. The existing generate:ascendant-glyph-icons command remains compatible and synchronizes both sets, so the current preparation and prebuild hooks also refresh them. The standard source resolver uses sibling Ascendant-Technology and Vanilla projects. ASCENDANT_TECHNOLOGY_PROJECT_PATH, VANILLA_PROJECT_PATH and BRIDGE_PROJECTS_PATH support other checkout layouts. Builds without these local sources retain the committed sprites. There is no runtime request to the addon directories or an external CDN.

Item and machine detail navigation: overview, specifications, recipes, drops, uses, related items, notes and mining sections. Player statistics: health, attack, damage reduction, critical stats, movement, energy, fluid/gas capacity, processing time, mining, enchantability, fuel and storage. Equipment catalogs and individual equipment pages: potion effects and immunities, including regeneration, poison, wither, hunger, blindness and darkness. Immunities retain their text and add a prohibition mark over the effect icon. Machine guides: catalyst slots, secondary outputs, schematic fluid/catalyst inputs, and the actual supported upgrade types. Energy, speed, Hyper, stack, range, filter and quantity upgrades use their respective glyphs. wikiUiIcons.mjs owns the paths and semantic mappings. Source labels are resolved before translation. This keeps English, Portuguese and Spanish on the same icon and avoids guessing an effect from an item name or description. For example, Bonus damage uses the attack glyph; Strength II uses the vanilla Strength effect. Unknown abilities use a neutral vector fallback. All images have explicit square dimensions, object-fit: contain, image-rendering: pixelated, empty alternative text and a decorative wrapper hidden from assistive technology. Adjacent labels remain readable and supply the accessible meaning. Immunity and effect labels remain distinct. Health values render the actual number of hearts: +3 followed by three heart sprites, +5 followed by five. Half-heart bonuses use the original half-heart sprite without rounding. The visible 9×9 heart inside each 16×16 source is framed with CSS at 1em, so its visible height follows the surrounding text instead of shrinking inside transparent margins. This exception uses a positioned image inside a clipped frame; the original PNG remains unchanged. The same component supplies stat cards, catalog benefits, related items and technical attribute values. Screen readers receive the full localized value once. An explicit Fire resistant: Yes item statistic renders a compact property badge with the vanilla Fire Resistance icon. It does not create a potion effect or player immunity in the data. Items and machines have one overview navigation entry; technical details remain collapsible there. Their existing /specs URLs remain valid and mark Overview as active. Blocks retain separate specifications because their sections have different content.

npm run test:wiki includes sprite presence, dimensions, transparency, semantic separation, fallback behavior, exact copying and preservation when source packs are unavailable, alongside the existing wiki data, localization and route tests. Browser review uses a focused production build; it does not replace a full publication build or physical-device testing. The initial implementation review compiled 14 representative routes in each of the three locales (42 HTML pages), retaining the full 21,608 generated route definitions for strict link checks. Subsequent layout corrections are reviewed first in a standalone HTML preview and then through the local development server, without repeating a production build for layout iteration. The current suite also covers repeated/fractional hearts, explicit fire-resistant flags and compatibility of old specifications routes. The 80 library sprites total 21,572 bytes and match their local pack sources byte-for-byte. Local mobile review uses simulated browser viewports, not a physical device.

The machinery library shared by UtilityCraft and its extensions. Build compatible machines, generators, resource storage, configurable IO, upgrades, and multiblocks without changing the Core. Get startedBrowse the API

DoriosCore is a JavaScript library for Minecraft Bedrock machinery addons. It supplies the common runtime used to create machines and generators that follow the same lifecycle and storage rules as UtilityCraft. It is appropriate to call this an API: the term refers to the public classes, functions, constants, and type contracts that addon scripts can use. It is not a web API and it does not make HTTP requests. MACHINERY Machines and generators Use runtime wrappers with scheduling, progress, energy, inventories, UI labels, preserved resources, and safe placement and destruction. RESOURCES Energy, liquids, and gases Store large values, create multiple indexed tanks, render resource displays, and transfer resources between compatible containers. CONFIGURATION IO and upgrades Expose six-face item, liquid, and gas controls and consume standard or addon-defined upgrade perks in your own processing logic. STRUCTURES Multiblocks Detect structures, activate controllers, calculate component-based stats, route through ports, and restore blocks during deactivation.
Use runtime wrappers with scheduling, progress, energy, inventories, UI labels, preserved resources, and safe placement and destruction.
Store large values, create multiple indexed tanks, render resource displays, and transfer resources between compatible containers.
Expose six-face item, liquid, and gas controls and consume standard or addon-defined upgrade perks in your own processing logic.
Detect structures, activate controllers, calculate component-based stats, route through ports, and restore blocks during deactivation.

Understanding the library boundary prevents incompatible addons and duplicated systems. Project Responsibility DoriosLib Global Dorios utilities and registries used across different projects. DoriosCore Machinery runtime: machine classes, resource storage, IO documents, UI interfaces, upgrades, scheduling, rotation, and multiblocks. UtilityCore UtilityCraft-owned systems, including machinery networks. DoriosCore does not own the networks. Your addon core Custom reusable behavior that extends DoriosCore, such as heat, pressure, radiation, or a specialized recipe cycle.

A Minecraft Bedrock project using the Script API versions supported by the current UtilityCraft manifest. UtilityCraft 3.5.0 or newer enabled in the world. DoriosLib and DoriosCore available through UtilityCraft. A script bundler or Regolith configuration that resolves the public library aliases. For a working starting point, clone the UtilityCraft Addon Template. It includes functional blocks, entities, screens, IO, upgrades, liquids, gases, generators, and multiblocks.

Treat the DoriosCore and DoriosLib dependency folders as read-only. Addons consume them; they do not patch them. BP/scripts/ ├─ DoriosCore/ # Dependency: do not modify ├─ DoriosLib/ # Dependency: do not modify ├─ ADDONNAME_CORE/ # Your reusable subclasses and systems ├─ config/ # Registrations and shared data ├─ examples/ # Concrete blocks and gameplay behavior └─ main.js # Load order and initialization When behavior does not belong in the shared machinery library, extend a public class in ADDONNAME_CORE: // BP/scripts/MYADDON_CORE/ThermalMachine.js import { Machine } from "DoriosCore/index.js"; export class ThermalMachine extends Machine { getHeat() { return Number(this.entity.getDynamicProperty("myaddon:heat") ?? 0); } setHeat(value) { this.entity.setDynamicProperty("myaddon:heat", Math.max(0, value)); } } See Extend DoriosCore for the complete pattern and rules.

Follow Get started to understand load order and create a machine runtime safely. Read Machine lifecycle before implementing processing logic. Learn how to extend DoriosCore without editing library code. Browse the complete API surface and open the reference page for the system you need. Compare your implementation with the public examples in the Addon Template, UtilityCraft, and Heavy Machinery.

UtilityCraft Heavy Machinery — multiblock controllers, components, and ports.
